core_condition: at least one measured effect recorded in observed_effects from Ventora telemetry or public corpora

evidence.rationale: Large and convergent. Reber, Schwarz & Winkielman (2004) established the fluency–preference link; Alter & Oppenheimer (2009) unified perceptual, linguistic and conceptual fluency findings; Schwarz (2004) set out the metacognitive account; Dechêne, Stahl, Hansen & Wänke (2009) meta-analysed the truth effect; Fazio et al. (2015) showed prior knowledge does not protect against illusory truth; Pennycook et al. (2018) demonstrated the effect for fake-news headlines. The corpus carries 100 records in the dissent category, which for once reflects a genuinely well-argued literature rather than noise. Grade A- rather than A because what the fluency signal *means* is interpretable and learnable, not fixed — see dissent.

product_applicability.rationale: Cross-cutting and immediately implementable: legibility, plain concrete language, familiar structure. Applies to every surface. Reference: plain-language pricing pages, government service-design standards, conventional checkout structure.

measurability.rationale: The consequences are reachable (conversion, completion, time-to-complete), but fluency itself is measured in the literature by contested instruments, and its effects are modest and easily confounded with the load and comprehension gains produced by the same design changes. Attributing an observed improvement specifically to fluency rather than to CL-14/MM-15 will be difficult in our telemetry — scored 2 honestly.

orthogonality.rationale: Sits close to CL-14 (load) and MM-15 (comprehension): the same design change typically moves all three. Retained as distinct because its claim is about *judgement consequences of ease* — liking, trust, perceived truth — which neither capacity nor comprehension addresses. Score 2 for real overlap.

safety.rationale: Lowest safety score in S7, and among the lowest in the whole registry — deliberately. This mechanism includes the illusory-truth effect: repeated or easily processed claims are judged more accurate irrespective of accuracy, and Fazio et al. showed that knowing better does not protect people. That is the cognitive basis of misinformation, and a product engine that treated it as a persuasion tool would be building a machine for making weak claims feel true. Three block-severity rules constrain it: no fluency applied to unsupported claims; no deliberate disfluency to obstruct (small-print terms, hard-to-read cancellation — specifically regulated); material information presented at least as fluently as promotional content. Admitted because the legitimate use — making genuinely true, genuinely valuable things easy to grasp — is exactly what good interface writing is, and because naming the hazard explicitly is safer than leaving it implicit in other mechanisms.

dissent: This mechanism's own literature contains the strongest correction to its naive reading. (1) The meaning of fluency is learned, not intrinsic: Unkelbach (2007) reversed the truth effect experimentally by training participants to interpret ease differently, and Briñol, Petty & Tormala (2006) showed the 'malleable meaning of subjective ease' — the same feeling can be read as validity, as familiarity, or as triviality depending on context and expectation. Fluency is therefore a signal whose interpretation is contextual, not a lever with a fixed direction. (2) Disfluency sometimes wins: Belke et al. (2015) found challenging, less fluent art can be preferred after processing effort, and boundary-condition work on disfluency and judgements of learning (Magreehan et al. 2016) shows the effect on metacognition is narrower than early claims. Difficulty can signal depth and can improve engagement where the audience expects substance. (3) Measurement: Graf, Mayer & Landwehr (2017) questioned how processing fluency is measured, finding single- and multi-item instruments diverge — which weakens quantitative claims. (4) Confounding, ours: because legibility and plain language simultaneously lower cognitive load and raise comprehension, an observed product improvement cannot cleanly be attributed to fluency; we should expect not to be able to separate PF-16's contribution from CL-14/MM-15 in our own measurement, and should not claim otherwise. The ethical caveat is not dissent but is recorded here for weight: the same evidence that makes this mechanism real (illusory truth surviving prior knowledge, prior exposure raising perceived accuracy of fake news) is the reason its guardrails are absolute rather than advisory.

Pennycook, Cannon & Rand (2018). Prior exposure increases perceived accuracy of fake news. JEP: General 147(12).

notes: Cross-checked against /corpora/evidence/PF-16.json (310 records; both pins resolved, though one prep pin DOI resolved to an unrelated primatology paper — the intended boundary work was located via terms and is cited correctly here). Corpus contains substantial genuine critique. Cross-cutting mechanism: parent S7. Total 11 sits at the admission threshold, driven by safety 1 and measurability 2 — this is the honest position for a mechanism that is scientifically strong, operationally entangled with its neighbours, and ethically the most hazardous in the node. Verdict INCUBATING; CORE strictly on a measured effect, with the caveat that attribution will be difficult.
